articleTitle: A Blockchain Based Data Auction Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
abstract: In the present digital era, data has become an increasingly valuable asset to both enterprises and society. Despite the vast amount of available data, the absence of a reliable means of transaction often hinders the direct benefits that data can bring. This results in a lack of willingness among data owners to conduct transactions, poor data mobility, and an inability to fully realize the value of data. In order to promote the transaction and circulation of data, this study proposes a data auction model based on blockchain technology, which ensures transparency, security, and efficiency in data auctions. Furthermore, an optimal auction algorithm is devised, which demonstrates that in the process of data trading with multiple participants, the auction model can maximize the utility of data owners, improve their willingness to trade, enhance data liquidity, fully realize the value of data, and provide a platform for sustainable development of data trading.

articleTitle: Single Image Dehazing Based on Deep Feature Fusion Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
abstract: Image dehazing can make images clearer and more realistic. The dehaze image is more easily recognized and understood by the human eye, and also helps to improve the performance of the computer vision system. Transformer has found significant application in image dehazing because of its remarkable ability to extract global features. However, employing Transformer solely in image dehazing often leads to the loss of image details, while CNN is ineffective in global feature extraction. Therefore, we integrated CNN and Transformer to enhance image dehazing. We introduced a novel technique to address the feature fusion dilemma by utilizing a transmission-guided map to extract haze-based photo characteristics, thereby uniting the features of CNN and Transformer. The combined features contain both image nuances and extensive-range data. Comprehensive tests indicate that our approach outperforms all others on numerous quality assessment metrics.

articleTitle: The Evaluation Method of Science and Technology Collaborative Innovation Based on Blockchain Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
abstract: Blockchain technology has significantly applicable value in technology collaborative innovation evaluation for its decentralization, tamper resistance, traceability, concealment, and openness. It forms the evaluation pattern at the theoretical framework level, builds an evaluation technical platform with blockchain technology, and establishes case demonstrations, effectively solving the bottleneck problems in information source timeliness, authenticity, and accuracy, which is encountered by traditional methods.

articleTitle: Trusted Searchable Cryptographic Authentication Model in Edge Computing
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
abstract: Edge computing is a new paradigm in which end users’ access to computing resources is constrained by their physical size. And where edge nodes in edge computing networks generate income by offering services like storage, computing resources, etc. Although end users and edge nodes desire more benefits with fewer resources, edge computing operates in a trustless environment. The current options either use an honest third party or a blockchain with high computational overhead authentication. To create a committee of witnesses to verify outsourced file search services, we propose a validation model that makes use of game theory and smart contracts. The witnesses are encouraged to provide truthful responses in the verification service by a payoff function created by the Nash equilibrium principle. To prevent collusion and a single point of failure, unbiased witness selection is also carried out using a witness randomization technique. Besides, a reputation mechanism for the witness’s behavior is created, and it will suffer if the witness acts sluggishly or irregularly. When its reputation value is below a set threshold, it is ineligible to participate in the witness selection process. The approach is put into practice using the Ethereum blockchain’s smart contracts, and experimental results show that it can work.

articleTitle: VulScan: A Vulnerability Detection Model Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
abstract: Ensuring software security requires effective identification of vulnerabilities in the source code, as they can make software systems susceptible to attacks. In recent years, deep learning techniques have emerged as promising approaches for vulnerability detection in source code. This paper introduces VulScan, a model that combines Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) to identify vulnerabilities. By representing the source code as an Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) and applying GCN to extract structural features, VulScan captures both the graph-based relationships and sequential information using BiLSTM. Comparative evaluations against baseline techniques commonly used in vulnerability detection demonstrate VulScan’s superior performance, leading to improved detection accuracy.

articleTitle: Split-Chain based Efficient Blockchain-Assisted Cross-Domain Authentication for IoT
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
abstract: The rapid development of network and manufacturing technologies has enabled a growing number of IoT devices to connect to the network. Like humans, these devices from different domains of the world also require interconnection, which necessitates identity authentication to ensure communication security and prevent cyber-attacks. To avoid the problem of single-point failure, there are existing cross-domain device authentication methods, many of which are based on blockchain. However, most schemes use a pre-existing blockchain architecture, and few people design customized blockchain solutions for cross-domain authentication scenes to improve the efficiency of authentication. In this paper, we present a split-chain based efficient authentication mechanism, SCBA, for cross-domain IoT. To improve the efficiency of authentication, we have designed an efficient blockchain structure that achieves high authentication. Additionally, we have designed a consensus algorithm that supports the above blockchain structure to ensure the security and fairness of the authentication system. Extensive experiments have been conducted to show that our scheme has significant advantages in terms of efficiency.

articleTitle: History-IP Filtering Based on Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
abstract: The power system is typically of great importance for a city’s regular functioning. In many cases, the slightest error in the power system seriously affects the safety, food, health and other infrastructure. Therefore, the security of the power system is crucial. In the past decade, most power systems have been upgraded and connected to the network. The security of power systems has evidently become a crucial component of network protection, with Distribution Denial of Service (DDoS) being one of the most frequent network assaults.DDoS attacks are distributed, deceptive, and covert, making it difficult to track and prevent.Attackers will forge the source IP address, attack the target, consume network bandwidth and system resources, and make normal services impossible. For a server, users who used to visit frequently are more trusted. Therefore, when DDoS occurs, providing priority services for these historical users can effectively resist attacks. In order to screen these users as easily and quickly as possible and establish a complete and reliable IP address database, we propose a history-IP filtering method based on neural network. Experimental results demonstrate the model’s aptitude for detecting assaults.

articleTitle: Study On Five-dimensional Chaotic System Based On Flux-controlled Memristor
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
abstract: Chaotic systems are widely used in communication systems because of their high sensitivity to initial values and their inherent properties of being random-like and broad-spectrum. In this paper, based on the four-dimensional LCL chaotic system, a new five-dimensional chaotic system is obtained by replacing the coupling parameters in the chaotic system using a controlled memristor and selecting suitable system parameters.The phase trajectory diagram, Lyapunov exponent diagram and bifurcation diagram of this system are plotted by MATLAB experimental simulations with one system parameter changed, and the basic dynamic characteristics, stability and chaotic properties of the system are analysed with the simulation results. The parameters in the memristor are used as control variables to analyse their effect on the offset increments, and the system is subjected to a NIST test to demonstrate the randomness of the sequence generated by the system. The circuit model is built using the basic module of simulink, and the simulated phase trajectory diagram and time domain diagram are compared with the images simulated by the MATLAB code to prove that the improved system is a hyper-chaotic system and that the system can be well applied to encryption in the field of communication.

articleTitle: Configuration Error Localization Based on Delta Debugging
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
abstract: User misconfiguration has become one of the leading causes of complex software failures in the cloud and data center. Once a vulnerability caused by misconfiguration occurs, effective software error localization technology is needed to help developers quickly find relevant code fragments to complete the repair. At present, software error localization technology mainly faces two challenges when it is applied to complex software in clouds and data centers. On the one hand, there are many configuration parameters input into the software, which makes it difficult to quickly locate the error configuration parameters; on the other hand, the complex composition of software function modules makes it difficult to locate the relevant error codes. To solve the above challenges, this paper proposes a configuration error localization technique based on delta debugging, which is based on the running results of unit tests. It includes two parts: error-configuration location technique based on dichotomous reset algorithm and error-code location technique based on execution comparison strategy. We tested our techniques on a complex cloud system software. The experimental results show that when the target configuration set size was 6 and the initial configuration set size was 20, the dichotomous reset-based algorithm improved the selection efficiency by 5.8x compared to the permutation-based algorithm with an accuracy rate of 98.6%. At the same time, the execution comparison-based strategy can be verified on the HADOOP-18362 in the real world, and the error code that leads to its configuration vulnerability can be located.

articleTitle: Research on GPU-Based Parallel Processing for the Paillier Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
abstract: The homomorphic encryption algorithm Paillier is a cryptographic method that can be applied in areas such as privacy-preserving computation and federated learning. However, due to the inherent complexity and computational overhead of the algorithm, it may affect real-time requirements when dealing with a large volume of encrypted data. In this paper, we propose a method to improve the efficiency of the encryption algorithm by combining GPU parallel processing technology with homomorphic encryption. Through experiments on encrypting and decrypting plaintexts of different sizes, the results show that the introduction of GPU significantly improves the encryption and decryption speed. Compared with other parallel processing methods, the acceleration effect of our proposed method is more significant.

articleTitle: Research on Information Security Assessment Method Based on Automated Testing
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
abstract: UI testing is an important part of software testing, as it provides testing integrity and can maximize the discovery of software quality issues. In the software testing process, information security is undoubtedly the most basic requirement. Currently, the most typical UI automation testing tools are Selenium and Uiautomator, where Selenium is mainly used for UI automation testing of web projects and Uiautomator is mainly used for UI automation testing of Android mobile apps. Using Selenium and Uiautomator for UI automation testing often involves simulating various user behaviors through automation scripts to operate the software and discover software vulnerabilities and security risks. During the testing process, the main issues involved are data security and code security. UI automation testing requires the use of real data for testing, such as user accounts, passwords, bank card numbers, and other sensitive information. If these are leaked or tampered with, it can lead to serious losses. Additionally, if there are code vulnerabilities in the testing script code itself, it can result in the testing results being tampered with, affecting the quality of the testing. To address these issues, this paper proposes applying OCR technology to UI automation testing. For sensitive data issues, OCR is used to recognize and obtain the information. For testing results, OCR technology is used to obtain the test result information on the screen. Practical tests have shown that applying OCR technology to actual project testing scenarios can effectively solve data security and code security issues in testing. This solution has high practical value.

articleTitle: Research on the System of Blockchain Data Sharing and Early-warning Decision for Public Health Emergency
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
abstract: The key of early prevention and control of infectious diseases is to use the early warning technology and system to monitor the abnormal occurrence and trend of infectious diseases. Based on the hospital data, this paper analyzes the patient demographics, syndromic features, and other sensitive medical characteristics, proposes an infectious disease risk warning algorithm based on dynamic adaptive modeling of event evolution, and constructs an infectious disease risk early warning and data sharing system based on blockchain technology. The proposed system realizes the safe storage and sharing of data throuth the blockchain technology, and combines smart contracts and federal learning to realize distributed risk warning and consensus decision making. The experiments demonstrate that the proposed risk warning model can improve infectious disease risk warning and fusion decision making by taking into account the requirements of warning accuracy and timeliness while protecting patient privacy.

articleTitle: A Network Vulnerability Assessment Method Based on Asset Weight
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
abstract: According to the characteristics of frequent node interaction and obvious differences in applications of marine network, this paper takes the degree of information interaction between assets as the basis for measurement. With the concept of logical edge number introduced, serial static and dynamic elements, such as upstream traffic, downstream traffic, number of logical edges, and number of applications, are taken as the evaluation indexes. Assigned values based on expert experience, the entropy weight method is applied to calculate and verify the comprehensive weight of network assets. According to the preset classification rules and CVSS vulnerability-scoring model, the vulnerability assessment of the virtual marine network is carried out. The results show that the selected indexes can calculate the weight of assets scientifically, and the method can provide a basis for the security optimization of the measured network.

articleTitle: Construction and FPGA Simulation Verification of Non-degenerate Five-Dimensional Hyperchaotic System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
abstract: In order to measure the relationship between the number of positive Lyapunov exponents and the degree of chaos in a better way, the concept of degeneracy is introduced in this paper. A new non-degenerate continuous time five -dimensional hyperchaotic system is constructed with the maximum number of positive Lyapunov exponents, which shows that the whole system has good chaotic properties. The system is implemented in an FPGA platform using Verilog programming language, which makes it easier to control the parameters and initial values of the system. In this paper, the top-down design concept is adopted to design and write the system functions, and the non-degenerate five-dimensional continuous time hyperchaotic system is simulated and verified in VIVADO FPGA hardware development platform. The simulation results are compared with the results obtained by MATLAB numerical simulation, and a method to solve the problem of data accuracy in the process of FPGA computing chaotic system is proposed. In order to provide a new implementation of hyperchaotic system based on FPGA.

articleTitle: State Tracking and Evaluation Technology for Big Data Objects Based on a New Digital Watermarking Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
abstract: Currently, enterprises generally face the following problems in managing big data: Multiple versions or replicas of the same data object cross-system interfaces, delayed data destruction with invalid data not being cleared in time, difficulty in tracking data with no support of data traceability technology, weak data security and insufficient risk analysis capabilities. To address these problems, this article proposes a new digital watermarking algorithm that is suitable for embedding digital watermarks in big data objects. Combined with flow data analysis technology, it can track and monitor the processes of generating, storing, transmitting, processing, and publishing big data objects, mark the version status of data objects, draw the distribution map of enterprise data status, we innovatively apply this recognition technology to calculate key indicators such as the health value of big data object references and the number of invalid data object references, and analyze data objects using predefined weaknesses and risk rules to discover data security issues and provide danger warnings for enterprises.

articleTitle: Blockchain-based ciphertext access control for data sharing using key encapsulation mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
abstract: The article presents a plan for distributing access control and data sharing through CP-ABE. This plan allows for provable security and privacy protection without requiring authorization agencies. The main key of the CP-ABE algorithm is managed in a distributed manner based on blockchain through proxy key encapsulation technology, and a blockchain dual-chain model is adopted to improve system performance and security. At the same time, the block structure and data format specifications are designed to achieve on-chain supervision with traceable management and operational behavior of the PKEM-CPABE algorithm. Experimental simulation analysis shows that the proposed algorithm achieves an efficient and secure sharing mechanism while protecting data privacy.

articleTitle: A Privacy-aware Electronic Medical Record Sharing Scheme based on Blockchain and Identity-based Cryptography
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
abstract: At present, blockchain has become the research focus in the field of medical information, especially in the storage and sharing of electronic medical records (EMR). With the advent of the era of big data, data privacy is particularly important for patients. However, in existing blockchain-based electronic medical record-sharing schemes, the transaction address in the blockchain is related, which poses the risk of privacy disclosure for patients. To to solve this problem, this paper proposes a privacy-aware sharing scheme of electronic medical records based on stealth address and smart contracts. We introduce a novel identity-based stealth address scheme that can ensure the privacy protection of patient data and avoid the complexity of certificate management under the PKI system. As far as we know, this is the first of its kind. The patient can control the data autonomously through a smart contract. We present the specific design process of the scheme and the security proof of the related algorithm. Compared with the existing schemes, the identity-based cryptosystem is more suitable for users. Meanwhile, the scheme uses the decentralized storage platform IPFS to store EMR data to avoid the limitations of centralized data storage.

articleTitle: Design and Research of Credit Sharing Model Based on Blockchain and Agent Re-encryption
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
abstract: The traditional credit investigation mode is often prone to data tampering and data leakage due to its centralized data storage, and once the data is damaged, it is difficult to recover the data, which will make the security of credit investigation data and personal privacy under serious threat. To solve the above problems, this paper proposes a credit-sharing scheme based on blockchain and agent re-encryption. Firstly, blockchain technology is used to solve the problems of data centralization, easy data tampering, easy data leakage, and other problems existing in traditional credit investigation platforms. Secondly, the SM2 encryption function is used to construct the proxy re-encryption algorithm, and the blockchain technology is combined to realize the safe sharing of credit data. Moreover, the interplanetary file system is used to effectively solve the problems of traditional credit centralized storage and the difficult recovery of data damage. Finally, the secure analysis and performance analysis show that this scheme not only realizes the security sharing of credit data but also has certain advantages in the aspect of computing cost.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Neural Network Model-based Approach for Detecting Smart Contract Vulnerabilities
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
abstract: Smart contract vulnerabilities have become a common source of security incidents in the blockchain network in recent years. To mitigate the impact of such vulnerabilities, scholars have been exploring more effective and dependable methods for detecting them. However, existing smart contract vulnerability detection methods suffer from issues like a high rate of false positives and omissions, limited scalability, and reliance on expert knowledge, among others. To address these challenges, this study proposes a hybrid neural network model-based approach to smart contract vulnerability detection that leverages the strengths of different neural networks. By incorporating global context alongside local feature extraction, the method significantly enhances feature extraction rates. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method is highly efficient and accurate, making it a suitable solution for detecting smart contract vulnerabilities.

articleTitle: A Multi-Party Collaboration Framework for Regulatory Compliance for Smart Contract Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
abstract: The increasing adoption of blockchain (BC) and smart contracts (SCs) in the financial sector necessitates effective regulatory compliance solutions that align with the decentralized nature of these systems. Existing centralized approaches to regulatory compliance face challenges in keeping pace with the rapidly evolving technology, creating potential gaps in enforcement. This paper proposes a MultiParty Collaboration Framework (MPCF) for Regulatory Compliance for SC Systems, a novel decentralized approach to integrating regulatory compliance directly into BC-based financial systems. This framework enables multi-party collaboration and enforces compliance with various regulatory requirements while preserving the core principles of decentralization. We present the design principles of the framework, its implementation and use cases. We also discuss the challenges, limitations, potential extensions, and future research directions. Our work contributes to the ongoing efforts to develop more robust and adaptable regulatory frameworks for BC-based financial systems, fostering innovation while ensuring compliance.

articleTitle: Secure voting system based on blockchain and threshold cryptography
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
abstract: Traditional electronic voting schemes based on blind signature often rely on fully trusted signature authorities, tally authorities, and face security threats. In this paper, threshold technology and privacy computing are used to realize decentralized data computing, decentralize the power of signature authorities and tally authorities; The blockchain technology is used to realize the function of electronic bulletin board and complete decentralized data storage, so as to ensure the openness and transparency of the whole election process. Furthermore, the proposed scheme is based on elliptic curve. Compared with the similar schemes based on bilinear pair, its computational complexity is reduced by an order of magnitude and has higher efficiency. Finally, this paper analyzes the security attributes and performance of the proposed scheme, and the experimental results of Python show that the proposed scheme has good performance in the optimized environment.

articleTitle: SIFT-based blockchain model for preventing the spread of forgery image
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
abstract: The detection of forgery images has become a hot issue in the field of communication. It is of great importance on researching how to prevent the uploading of forged images from the source of propagation. Blockchain can effectively protect the original features of images through distributed ledgers, consensus algorithms, asymmetric encryption, and smart contracts. Therefore, this paper proposes an idea of preventing the forgery images from the very beginning on the basis of blockchain, which aims at storing the original images into the blockchain through interaction with smart contracts. Our method not only provides safe and traceable copyright protection to the owners of the original images but also effectively suppresses the uploading of forgery images. Firstly, image features are extracted by Scale-invariant feature transform algorithm(SIFT) for image to be uploaded, the features are further matched by Fast Library for Approximate Nearest Neighbors(FLANN) with with the stored images in the blockchain. Secondly, the similarity between images is calculated in order to determine the originality of uploaded images, the ones with high similarity scores are refused to upload into the blockchain. At the same time, the copyright owner of the infringed image will be informed immediately. Finally, a large number of simulation results show that the method proposed in this paper can effectively authenticate the image copyright and prevent the spread of forgery images.

articleTitle: Research on the Reasoning Credibility of Privacy Infringement Risk Monitoring System Based on Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
abstract: As privacy protection policies continue to be strengthened, regulators are imposing harsher penalties for privacy infringement incidents. Driven by the profit factor, companies naturally wish to conceal and not report personal privacy infringements in their organizations. Therefore, it is crucial to ensure the credibility of the evidential data obtained by the privacy infringement risk monitoring system and the models and rules of the inference framework employed. In this paper, we analyze various factors affecting the inference trustworthiness of the privacy infringement risk monitoring system in cross-domain scenarios, propose improvement measures and methods to improve the inference trustworthiness of the system, define quantitative indicators and technical requirements for the design of the inference trustworthiness of the system based on the CF model, and verify the effectiveness of the inference trustworthiness design method of the privacy infringement risk monitoring system in cross-domain scenarios.

articleTitle: Blockchain-based Authentication Scheme for Vehicle Network Nodes
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
abstract: Internet of Vehicles (IoV) has developed into a useful service platform between vehicles and other vehicles, vehicles and roadways, and vehicles and pedestrians as a result of advancements in communication technology. However, along with the intelligent and networked IoV, IoV security issues are increasingly emerging, which often lead to extremely serious consequences. For example, when a vehicle is remotely attacked and maliciously controlled, it can lead to user privacy leakage. Attackers can also control the driving of vehicles through attacks, and there may even be a large number of connected cars being controlled in bulk, ultimately causing major social security incidents. In the Internet of Vehicles, authentication technology is one of the main solutions to address the security issues of the Internet of Vehicles. Many researchers have conducted some research on the authentication technology of vehicular network, but the traditional authentication scheme under the centralized system has problems such as frequent single-point failures and high overhead. When blockchain technology is properly implemented to the vehicle network environment, its security outperforms that of centralized systems due to features like decentralization, tamper-proof, security, and traceability. Because of this, we construct an optimization technique based on the Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance (PBFT) algorithm in this work and present an efficient IoV decentralized authentication scheme based on the consensus algorithm of blockchain technology. After performance analysis, it is proved that our scheme has better performance and higher security.

articleTitle: A Study of Data Augmentation for Imbalance Problem in Network Traffic
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
abstract: The complexity and diversity of smart grid systems increase the likelihood of anomalies in communications between devices in the system, and how these anomalies are detected is critical to the security of the grid system. However, the distribution of traffic types in the grid is often highly unbalanced, with the total amount of normal traffic data often far outweighing the anomalous data. This imbalance compromises the effectiveness of the detection model and poses a significant threat to the overall security of the grid. This paper improves on traditional conditional generation adversarial neural networks and designs a new approach to overcome this obstacle and enhance the security of smart grid systems. In the generator part, the spatial features of the data are captured by convolutional neural networks, and the temporal features of the data are captured by gated recurrent units. By integrating these two components into the generative network, we can generate synthetic data with both temporal and spatial features, thus enhancing the minority class samples. By incorporating the augmented minority data into the training process, the proposed approach enables the detection model to understand the distribution of features of the minority anomaly samples more accurately. This improved learning accuracy translates into improved model performance, resulting in higher detection rates for previously under-represented anomalies. In addition, our approach effectively addresses the inherent bias towards traffic types with higher flows typically observed in asymmetric datasets, thus providing a more equitable and comprehensive security solution for smart grid systems.

articleTitle: Enhancing IoT Security and Privacy through Blockchain Technology, Reinforcement Learning, and Constitutional AI
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
abstract: The rapid growth of the Internet of Things (IoT) has brought significant benefits to various industries, but it also poses new challenges in terms of security and privacy protection. In this paper, we propose a novel approach to enhance IoT security and privacy by combining blockchain technology with reinforcement learning algorithms and Constitutional Artificial Intelligence (CAI). This approach enables secure data storage and access control, adaptive data provenance and integrity, and adaptive identity management in IoT networks. We introduce Reinforcement Learning from Artificial Intelligence Feedback (RLAIF) and CAI to make the system adaptive and intelligent. RLAIF allows the system to learn from AI-generated feedback signals and make adjustments to its security mechanisms, while CAI ensures that the system adheres to the principles and guidelines set forth in a constitution, prioritizing user privacy and security. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, paving the way for more secure and privacy-preserving IoT networks.

Author Keywords: Reinforcement Learning from Artificial Intelligence Feedback(RLAIF)

articleTitle: DPIS: Blockchain Makes Personal Information Safer
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
abstract: This paper provides an in-depth analysis of the current state of personal information storage and usage, as well as the existing issues in this domain. It proposes an architecture for building a decentralized, self-organizing, and scalable personal information service system. By improving the organization of the blockchain and constructing a circular access structure, the storage and usage of personal information leverage blockchain technology and cryptographic techniques to enhance the system’s availability and reliability. The article elaborates on the various components of the system and their operational mechanisms, as well as the process for personal information query and authorization for use. The implementation and benchmarking results show the proposed architecture has significant performance advantage comparison with other main stream blockchain for safe date exchange. The proposed architecture balances the use of personal information with security protection, offering a standardized, secure, and convenient approach for personal information usage.

articleTitle: IoV Edge Data Integrity Audit Method Based on Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
abstract: With the quick development of Internet of Vehicles (IoV) technology, a lot of private data of vehicle users has been generated. An increasing amount of vehicle data is being collected in the cloud storage providers (CSP) and the edge node (EN). These data involve user privacy and vehicle driving data, and once they are damaged or lost, they wm lead to serious traffic accidents. Therefore, safeguarding the security and integrity of IoV data has become a hot issue. However, due to the distributed nature of the IoV data system and the difficulty of edge node management, the traditional data integrity auditing methods can no longer satisfy the needs in the IoV cloud-edge collaboration scenario. Therefore, we propose a IoV edge data integrity audit method based on blockchain First, our design a novel cloud-edge collaborative storage model that not only allows both cloud and edge to participate in the audit, but also enables the data user (DU) to quickly access the IoV data and reduce the pressure of data transmission. Second, during the audit phase, we use the third-party auditor (TPA) to design a low-overhead audit algorithm and ensure that the privacy of the IoV data is not compromised. Finally, the TPA records audit transactions on the blockchain, so that the DU can re-review the TPA’s audit results to find out whether the TPA is delaying and falsifying the audit result. Theoretical analysis shows that our method can protect the privacy of IoV data. Meanwhile, the experimental results show that our method has a low time overhead and the storage model is suitable for the IoV environment.

articleTitle: Graph-based Analysis of the Algorand Blockchain Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
abstract: Over the past few years, Algorand has emerged as one of the prominent pure proof-of-stake (PPoS) blockchains, with a rapidly growing number of accounts and transactions. Despite its increasing significance, there is limited knowledge about its smart contracts, transaction activities, and other features. This paper presents the first comprehensive study of Algorand using graph analysis to investigate the creation of entities, payment of Algos, invocation of smart contracts, and transfer of assets over time. By collecting and analyzing external transaction data, we have constructed graphs to gain insights into the behavior of the blockchain. Our research has uncovered novel observations and insights by performing relevant graph analysis, and we have also proposed a solution to one security problem based on these graphs.

articleTitle: Blockchain storage space optimization method based on knowledge granularity-neighborhood rough entropy feature selection algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
abstract: Blockchain is a distributed database with tamper-evident and decentralized data structure. However, due to the huge amount of data in blockchain, the storage costs are is high. In an effort to minimize data storage expenses, it is necessary to choose the most pertinent data features for preservation on the blockchain. Therefore, an effective data feature selection method can quickly and accurately select the most representative data features, which can reduce the redundancy of blockchain upload data features and effectively confirm rights. This paper puts forth a feature selection algorithm (i.e. FS_NGRE) based upon the neighborhood granularity rough entropy and firefly algorithm (abbreviated to FA) to select representative data features, effectively decreasing the cost of storing data on the blockchain. Furthermore, the public datasets are employed for simulated testing. The results of these trials demonstrates that the proposed feature selection algorithm surpassed alternative feature selection strategies in the matter of accuracy, facilitating the selection of more significant features while diminishing the scale of the feature set. The proposed methodology can serve as an effective means for verifying the integrity of data stored on the blockchain.

articleTitle: Exploring the Impact of Non-IID on Federated Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
abstract: In the past few years, the growing problem of data silos has given rise to an emerging framework for distributed deep learning: Federated learning. The framework enables the construction of global models across multiple participants without the need for directly sharing raw data. However, because the environments oriented towards Federated learning are usually complex and heterogeneous, resulting in varying degrees of data distribution among individual local devices, the distribution of data usually does not satisfy the assumption of non-independent and identically distributed. In this paper, several different types of non-independent and identically distributed datasets are obtained by dividing the MNIST dataset using various methods. Each dataset is then trained using the FedAvg algorithm to explore the effects of different datasets on the training of Federated learning models. It is finally concluded that in the process of Federated learning training, when the non-independent and identically distributed dataset contains partially independent and identically distributed data, a better training model can be obtained by appropriately adjusting the training parameters of the model. This paper also introduces the process of parameter debugging and analyzes the model training results under different parameters to improve the efficiency of Federated learning training models.

articleTitle: A Cross-Chain Identity Authentication Scheme for WSNs Based on Relay Chain
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) have been widely employed in the electric power industry, such as for power production data monitoring and power distribution data collection, due to their low overhead and swift deployment. Nonetheless, the massive data exchange requirements in the energy sector pose a tremendous challenge to data security. To address this issue, this paper proposes a multi-chain based authentication scheme for WSNs, wherein the WSNs are divided into numerous local private blockchains according to regions and cross-chain technology is utilized for scalability and global authentication requirements of the devices. In addition, fog computing nodes, located at the edge of WSNs, are utilized to make up for the inadequate computing powers for blockchain deployment and decrease data transmission latency. Through experiments, the security, attackresistance, throughput, and latency of the proposed scheme were evaluated. The results demonstrate that the proposed scheme guarantees anonymity, security, and Confidentiality and is applicable for deployment in WSNs systems.

articleTitle: Blockchain-Based Payment Channel Network: Challenges and Recent Advances
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
abstract: Blockchains, introduced in 2008, have garnered significant attention from both academia and industry. Cryptocurrencies, such as Bitcoin, which rely on blockchains, have great commercial value. However, the transaction processing speed of blockchains falls short of the traditional financial system. To address this, payment channels have emerged as a promising research direction for improving blockchain system performance by reducing transaction acknowledgment delay and enhancing transaction throughput. Payment channel networks facilitate a large number of transactions to be executed off-chain, preserving asset security, reducing costs, and promoting blockchain scalability. Among payment channel networks, Lightning Network is deployed on Bitcoin and has demonstrated efficient performance and high economic benefits in actual operations, attracting significant attention and research. This paper systematically analyzes the research outcomes of payment channel networks, focusing on the potential attacks and development direction of Lightning Network. Existing research is refined into security attacks, privacy vulnerabilities, and challenging system assumptions while exploring and comparing recent solutions in Lightning Network. Finally, this paper emphasizes the potential of payment channel networks, identifies the challenges that need to be addressed, and advances the study of blockchain payment channel networks.

articleTitle: Payment Channel Network Optimization Composed of Merkle Tree with Election Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Blockchain Technology and Information Security (ICBCTIS)
abstract: On-chain methods fail to improve the scalability of cryptocurrencies since they are constrained by block size and block creation rate. As a result, Payment Channel Networks (PCNs) have surfaced as a vital off-chain alternative for achieving scalability. In our prior research, we introduced a scheme called Accountable Assertions Performance optimization (A<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>PO) designed to identify malicious users in PCNs while optimizing computational efficiency and maintaining security. The original A<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>PO scheme assumed the third-party supervisor to be trustworthy; however, the potential for malicious behavior exists in reality. Consequently, we present an improved A<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>PO framework that incorporates an election mechanism. Supervisors for each transaction are automatically elected by calculating user balances. We offer a thorough security analysis, as well as the results of our evaluation show that the suggested scheme keeps the original A<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>PO’s benefits in terms of computing performance while enhancing security to thwart hostile supervisor operations.
